newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Paranagua port confident strike will end today.
newsitem.headline: Paranagua port confident strike will end today.

text.p: A strike at the key Brazilian port of Paranagua is likely to end between 1400 and 1500 local/1700 and 1800 GMT, with port operators and dockworkers privately saying they will cut a deal over pay, the port authority said.
"The strike should end today between 1400 and 1500," said a spokeswoman.

The port operators' union SINDOP is due to meet at 1100 local to consider a new proposal by the dockworkers, who are demanding a 21 percent wage increase. The port authority said SINDOP was very likely to approve the document.
"It is practically a done deal," the spokeswoman said.
Other workers at the port, including those at the export terminal which handles grains, went on strike at midday on Wednesday to support the dockworkers' demand.
Asked why the strike would end in the afternoon, rather than at midday, the spokeswoman said she had received the information from an official in the dockworkers' union.
SINDOP on Wednesday said the strike was costing the port $3 million per day. The port authority declined to put a figure on the cost of the strike.
